## 2024-08-06 - Memory Leak in String Truncation
**Learning:** Taking a sub-slice of a string generated by `hex.EncodeToString` (e.g., `hex.EncodeToString(h)[:12]`) keeps the entire original 64-byte backing array alive in memory, causing a memory leak for cached hashes.
**Action:** Always encode only the required prefix into a precisely-sized stack-allocated buffer (e.g., `var dst [12]byte`, `hex.Encode(dst[:], h[:6])`) and cast it directly to a string to avoid allocations and leaks.
